findings.title: Blocked email check is exact-match only and not normalized
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries with where(email: email) using the raw value, and neither this model nor EmailValidator strips or downcases the address. Discourse otherwise treats emails case-insensitively in several places, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace. The table/model also allow duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. This defeats the blocked-email enforcement.

findings.title: Domain allow/block regex is unanchored and can be bypassed
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds an unanchored, case-insensitive regular expression from the site setting. With a whitelist of allowed.com, an address such as user@allowed.com.attacker.com still matches because the regex does not anchor the domain to the end of the email. This allows email-domain whitelist restrictions to be bypassed; blacklist behavior can also overmatch unintended domains.

findings.title: Blocked-email validation writes match statistics during model validation
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? is a predicate that also increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record. EmailValidator calls it during User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so the same email can be counted multiple times for one request, and counts are updated even when the user record is ultimately invalid or not saved. This makes validation non-idempotent and corrupts the blocked-email statistics.

findings.title: Match counter is incremented in Ruby and saved non-atomically
findings.body: should_block? reads a BlockedEmail row, performs record.match_count += 1, and then saves it. Concurrent validation attempts can read the same match_count and overwrite each other's increments, losing statistics. Save failures are also ignored while the method still returns the block decision. An atomic counter update would be needed for reliable statistics.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is a mutable array defined on the controller prototype
findings.body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined in the controller class body, so the mutable array is shared rather than initialized per instance. pushObject mutates this shared state, and it is not reset when the create-account modal is reopened. Previously rejected emails can persist across controller instances or modal sessions and incorrectly invalidate a later form.

findings.title: Validator specs stub BlockedEmail and omit security-relevant cases
findings.body: The EmailValidator spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and does not cover the whitelist/blacklist regex, case/whitespace normalization, or actual interaction with BlockedEmail records. Because this PR centralizes security-relevant email blocking logic, these untested paths can regress or remain bypassable without detection.
